He has a slightly arched nose, sharp jaw, high cheekbones, dimple on right corner of lips and buttchin. He speaks victorian english and is 120+ years old. DIO is wears a black sleeveless, tight, tanktop. He has dark shade of butter colored unbuttoned cowboy chaps pants that is lowered over to his thighs while the hem of his black boxers appeared fron his hips. Long dark crimson suspenders unworn, dark grey vambraces, dark chocolate colored ankle boots with dark silver straps wrapped around knees with a grey kite knee guards. He has a shoulder length unkempt messy golden blond hair, a few strands slightly floating in mid air, slightly large strands on the sides of the face, two large strands on each left and right temple falling on face, creating split bangs that is arched, slightly tilted and is slightly above the eyes.

Naturally, Dio is an exceedingly-selfish person, only looking over his own interest and disregarding those of others at best, crushing them on the ground at worst. Owing to his composed nature, Dio can and will exploit and take what he can from all sorts of people, using any method, as long as the person suits his present desires because he is chiefly interested in their capabilities. Dio is the sort who is incapable of loving another person sincerely. The only people he can be said to have held some sort of affection for were Jonathan Joestar.

His natural cruelty is revealed very early when he schemes to exploit the Joestar family despite them being kind enough to adopt him. In order to place himself in a better position to supplant Jonathan Joestar and obtain the Joestar family fortune, Dio used the most dishonourable means to break him mentally. These methods included: humiliating Jonathan in public sport fighting, alienating him from his friends, and finally stealing Erina Pendleton’s first kiss to drive a wedge in their budding relationship. When he is eventually thwarted, Dio opted to slowly poison George Joestar I and slay Jonathan with the Stone Mask to make both deaths seem natural and accidental. Dio has shown a remarkable resolution to reach his goal, never losing his drive despite the numerous defeats he suffers throughout Phantom Blood and always tried to find a way to get back at Jonathan for them.

Dio’s lack of sympathy is also evident, since despite having lived for years with the kind Joestars, he never thought of them as anything more than hindrances, and is insinuated to utterly detest the upper class he frequents. Dio had been maintaining a facade of a charming and agreeable person to everyone save Jonathan, yet never came close to anyone. At the end of the part, the only person Dio appreciated was Jonathan Joestar himself, reluctantly admitting his valour as his archenemy.

When conversing with any one, Dio will evermore seek to beguile them and win them to his part, using a semblance of meekness and his native grace to make people esteem and favour him. For example, he played the pattern son and well-liked winsome friend to Jonathan’s father and company to better estrange him.

He is the sort who would be content with a man or woman; howbeit, he will do aught to get what he desireth and would utterly never bestow all of his love upon a certain person.

About a year after gaining his Stand, DIO discovered its signature ability of staying time. At first, he could only do this for a very short amount of time, but by the end of Part 3, he is able to stay time for a maximum of 9 seconds. This duration would have continued to increase, had DIO not been vanquished. When staying time, DIO giveth the impression that he is teleporting or otherwise moving at impossible speeds.

To give himself an advantage, DIO hath tried to keep the ability of The World a secret, only using it at key moments to daunt an opponent and perform unfathomable stealth attacks, as well as only trusting its secret to a few confidants such as Enya the Hag and not hesitating to eliminate her as soon as she remotely risked to inform the Joestars of his timestay power. However, as soon as they understood its ability, DIO dropped the secret and showed a great degree of confidence about the supremacy of his power, ultimately not caring about his secret as he was persuaded that no one could do aught about it. Thus, he began to liberally stay time against Jotaro. Thanks to the free time-frame of action granted by The World, DIO hath made it possible to instantly reposition himself to avoid attacks or set himself up to attack, kill enemies instantly, or even displace his opponents to toy with them.

Dio was born in the north-eastern part of London about the year 1867 or 1868 to Dario Brando, a drunken and cruel father whom he secretly abhorred—for he had inflicted much sorrow upon his mother. For a decade, Dio dwelt in misery and was thrashed by his father, enduring the loss of his mother. One day, as Dio attempted to administer medicine to his father, Dario struck him for not procuring the liquor he desired and bade him to sell his dead mother’s gown to purchase more spirits. Loathing and wrathful, Dio resolved to covertly slay his father with a poison he obtained from Wang Chan, learning from his expiring father of George Joestar’s obligation and instructed to exploit and appropriate the Joestar fortune. Dio encountered Jonathan Joestar immediately upon his arrival at the Joestar Mansion and instantly provoked him by kicking his dog, Danny. Unmoved by Jonathan, Dio commenced his scheme to break Jonathan's spirit through mental torture. Firstly, Dio maltreated Jonathan behind George Joestar I's back, for instance thrashing him, taunting him or pilfering his belongings. Nonetheless, Jonathan discovered happiness when he became Erina Pendleton's sweetheart. Dio, in a wicked design to dishonour Erina, did forcibly snatch from her the first kiss that should have been reserved for her true love, and boasted of his vile deed. But his triumph was short-lived, for Erina, in a gesture of defiance, did cleanse herself with the muddy water that lay on the road, thus implying that his kiss was naught but filth. This did enrage Dio so much that he struck her with his hand. His scheme, however, did recoil upon himself, for Jonathan soon heard of it. In a fury, JoJo did confront Dio. Dio had the upper hand at first, but Jonathan found the courage to thrash him soundly, making him weep like a child. Dio then drew a knife, but George came in and stopped the brawl, and chastised the boys severely. During the scuffle, Dio observed that a Stone Mask on the wall of the mansion had sprouted spikes, but he gave it little heed. Later, Dio bound Danny and put him in a box, and threw him in the mansion’s furnace, so that the butler unwittingly burned the poor dog. Yet Dio saw that Jonathan had a strong spirit, and knew that his plan had failed. Seven years thence, both lads did attend Hugh Hudson Academy, where Dio did aspire to graduate as a topmost law student. Their studies were crowned by a rugby match where Jonathan and Dio did cooperate to score a vital try. Dio did speak of friendship in front of the university's reporters but in his heart he still abhorred Jonathan. During that seven-year span, he had feigned brotherliness and friendliness toward Jonathan to beguile him into a false sense of security. Now a grown man, Dio did resolve to make his move and take the Joestar fortune by secretly poisoning George with the same poison he used to slay Dario. Jonathan did discover Dio's plot after reading Dario's letter to his father and did confront his half-brother as he brought another dose of poison to George. Jonathan did take the dose and Dio did try to stop him and did aver that he was putting their friendship in jeopardy. Dio, resolved to stop him, did scheme to slay Jonathan by contriving an accident with the Stone Mask. But upon hearing that Jonathan had entered Ogre Street, Dio did muse that he would not have to kill Jonathan himself. While roaming the streets of Liverpool, Dio was still uneasy and did drink from the bottle, loathing himself. Dio did find Jonathan waiting for him. Dio did attempt to stall by pleading but Robert E. O. Speedwagon and a band of constables did appear to arrest him for attempted murder. Beset and with naught left to lose, he did attempt to slay Jonathan but did inflict a mortal stab wound to George instead and did use his blood to activate the Stone Mask. Later, Jonathan kicks the walls, skewering him on a statue of the goddess of love; the combination of such a grievous wound and the surrounding fire overwhelms Dio, who apparently burns away. However, a few days hence when Wang Chan visits the burnt remnants of the house to find items to sell for lucre, Dio emerges and drains his blood while swearing revenge against Jonathan. After enlisting Jack the Ripper, Dio moves to the rural hamlet of Windknight’s Lot where he feeds on the populace to heal his body while building an army of zombies with the intent to take over London. Having sent Wang Chan to slay the supposed still convalescing Jonathan, Dio is astonished when Wang Chan returns injured and learns of the only thing besides sunlight that can destroy him: The Ripple. Two weeks later, Dio's head infiltrates the cruise ship the newly married Jonathan and Erina use to travel to America and celebrate their honeymoon. Hidden in a booby-trapped coffin, Dio has Wang Chan cause a zombie epidemic on the ship to lure Jonathan to him. Once making himself known to Jonathan while admitting to having an epiphany that their fates are deeply intertwined, Dio reveals his intention to take Jonathan's body as his own. Dio then shoots beams of eye humor at Jonathan's throat in an attempt to instantly kill him, but the attack only fatally wounded Jonathan with his stopped breathing preventing him from using his Ripple. Regardless, Jonathan uses his remaining Ripple to sabotage the ship to explode in a final attempt to end Dio for good. After putting Erina inside the coffin to protect her from the engine's explosion, Jonathan holds Dio's head in his arms. Dio begs Jonathan to let him live while tempting him with eternal life but realizes too late that Jonathan had died. The sinking ship explodes, though Dio succeeds in taking Jonathan's body and sinks into the depths of the Atlantic Ocean. 

In the year of our Lord 1884, the coffin of the accursed Dio was retrieved from the African shore by fortune-seekers, who were doubtless slain by his unholy hand anon. Dio then wandered far and wide, from the land of the Pharaohs to the Orient. In the month of July 1884, he sired a bastard son by a Japanese wench, who was named Giorno Giovanna. In the following year or two, he also begot another illegitimate offspring by a different mother, who was called Donatello Versus. In the year of our Lord 1886, he encountered the crone Enya and acquired a supernatural faculty, The World, by means of the Bow and Arrow. Dio had his lackey discharge a blunderbuss at him to assay The World's might and celerity. When The World endeavoured to seize the pellets, Dio perceived that time had ceased for an instant. Ere long, Dio enhanced his faculty further and could arrest time for longer, as he sensed the wheels of time and The World became conjoined with each other.Anon that year, Dio met Jean Pierre Polnareff and bewitched him. In the year of grace 1887, he first encountered Enrico Pucci whilst lurking in a church awaiting the sunset. DIO cured Pucci's deformed foot and bestowed him a Stand Arrow, discoursing about the gravity which unites people. He then bade Pucci to find him using the Arrow if he desired to know more. Circa 1887 to 1888, he sired the future mothers of Ungalo and Rikiel. In July 1888, he proceeded to meet Muhammad Avdol in Egypt. In August, he came across Noriaki Kakyoin whilst the latter was holidaying in Egypt and bewitched him also. After a train of mishaps that resulted in Pucci being pierced by the Arrow and gaining a Faculty, he turned to DIO. The pair would pass a good deal of time together, each journeying to the other's abode across the globe and debating how to turn their doctrines into reality. During one of DIO's calls, he abruptly broached his interest in attaining a perfect heaven, disclosing that he had penned the schemes to do so in a ledger and that he would require Pucci's aid in doing so. However, DIO doubted Pucci's fidelity to him, musing why the latter didn't use Whitesnake to extract The World from him. Pucci expounded that he loved DIO as he loved God, and thus revered him too much to betray him. Securing that he wouldn't wholly vanish, DIO left one of Jonathan's bones in Pucci's charge. The roused Dio Brando, now styled as "DIO", commences his next schemes within the latter months of 1888. For much of this time, DIO lurks in shadows and the enigma of precisely what his faculty "The World" does is a mystery to the Joestars and their associates. DIO's aspiration is to fashion a flawless world for him and his minions. In the meantime, he seeks to drain for himself the blood of the Joestar lineage, which will aid him to fully merge with Jonathan's body and take better command of The World. Despite his cognizance that Joseph Joestar and allies are seeking him, he does not make any endeavour to go encounter them himself and instead elects to abide in his mansion reading or feeding on the blood of women.
